topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: When optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals, the choice of satellite type (LEO or GEO) significantly impacts antenna aperture size trade-offs. LEO satellites require smaller apertures due to their lower altitude and faster movement, which reduces cost but increases interference. In contrast, GEO satellites use larger apertures with higher gain, providing broader coverage at higher costs. Frequency considerations also play a crucial role, as higher frequencies (e.g., Ka-band) require larger apertures for adequate gain in LEO satellites, while lower frequencies (e.g., S/C-band) are used in GEO satellites. Polarization diversity and radiation pattern optimization further complicate trade-offs by adding design complexity without direct budgetary impact but enhancing SNR and data rate.
